done.why: I died in the grue lair and lost my items. The two remaining ways forward were the cracked rock by the Great Door and the dark passage south of the lake. The first needed something bigger than a push, and I may have wasted the vial's liquid. The second needed a repellent I never found.

about: A Zork-style underground empire. After a dream-vision of an old man who says this is the final test, you explore caverns, a shadowy land, a cliff, an ocean, a lake and a great hall. The aim seems to be reaching the old man, past tests and obstacles that each want a particular object or trick.

ending.what: I did not reach an ending. I died in the grue lair, was revived at the stair, and got no further.

moments.note: Tying the rope to the chest let the unseen man haul it up, and I heard him open it and count coins. It was a clever reactive scene.
I was stranded on the ledge and the man never sent the rope back. I had to scramble down, which cost me the chest.
The sailor hinted at a greeting and 'say hello, sailor' worked. He gave me the vial.
The vial's liquid had no obvious use. Pouring it on the cracked rock and throwing the vial did nothing.
'drop all' also emptied the vial's liquid, which I may have needed.
I went south into the dark passage and was eaten by grues. The warning text was cryptic and I read it too late.

wished: A clearer hint about what the heavy liquid was for.
A way to get back up the cliff.
To find the repellent the text mentioned for the grue lair.

lines.line: I have waited three ages for someone to say those words and save me from sailing this endless ocean.
lines.why: A satisfying payoff to the sailor riddle.

lines.line: All at once, the chest is lifted from you.
lines.why: The world reacted to my action with a character who has his own agenda.

lines.line: Oh, no! Dozens of lurking grues attack and devour you!
lines.why: This was the death that sent me back to the start.

fun.why: Good puzzles and clever reactions, but I got stuck and lost items.

engagement.why: I was motivated to push toward the old man, and each area offered a hook.

difficulty.why: The hints were oblique and a death scattered my items.

interestingness.why: It has a varied map and NPC interactions, and echoes of classic games.

prose.why: Evocative room text and distinctive atmospheric warnings.
